collection source: an awaited call (query, request, or listing)

network request — api.post at line 12
no bound visible: no `.slice()` or `take`/`limit` on the source, no batching, no concurrency-limit helper, no semaphore

findings.summary: A retry wraps `stripe.refunds.create` with no idempotency or deduplication key visible at the call site. If an attempt succeeds but the response is lost, the retry applies the operation a second time.
evidence: retry construct: retry helper: withRetry(…) (line 26)
retried mutation — stripe.refunds.create at line 26 (name suggests a write)
boundary: payment (matched on `stripe`) — a duplicate here is visible to the customer, not just to the logs
safeguards visible at this site:
bounded attempt count: retry helper bounded at 5 attempt(s)
missing safeguard (primary): no idempotency or deduplication key — nothing lets the receiver recognise a replayed attempt as the same operation
also absent: error classification, delay or backoff, jitter, timeout or cancellation, transaction or atomic operation
attempt bound: 5
confidence 0.68 = 0.62 base + 0.08 (retry construct is explicit in this file) + 0.06 (operation touches payment) - 0.08 (mutation recognised by name only)
severity raised by: every failure is retried, including permanent ones, no delay or backoff between attempts, payment operation
findings.fix_shape: pass a stable idempotency key, or make the retry read-only

suggested_actions.description: Pass a stable idempotency key derived from the business operation (the order id, not a fresh UUID per attempt) so the provider collapses replays into one charge.
Retry only failures that can succeed on a second attempt. Replaying a 400 or a validation error just repeats it.
Add backoff between attempts, with jitter if many clients retry the same dependency at once.
